experiment.ground_truth_rule: A cached result must invalidate iff the mutated topology plane is in the query's declared dependency set; SEMANTIC is always bound.

coarse_all_four_planes.key: current key + all four topology fingerprints

typed_scoped_planes.key: current key + exact declared topology-plane fingerprints

finding: Under a deliberately stable state/execution/delivery generation, a V1.1-like cache key cannot distinguish mutations to active, coordination or physical topology. Binding all four planes is safe but over-invalidates. A typed dependency-scope key exactly separated required from irrelevant invalidations in this synthetic declared-dependency model.
hypothesis: Compiler-visible topology read effects plus scoped plane fingerprints close a real class of stale-rewrite/cache hazards more precisely than a universal all-topology generation fence.
counterhypothesis: In the actual Frank runtime every materially relevant topology mutation may already advance state_epoch or another single generation counter, making plane-scoped fingerprints redundant.
next_falsifier: Run current Frank/GWT/Hyperposition traces and mutate active gating, coordination lease/invariant topology and physical placement independently while holding semantic topology fixed. Compare current epoch-only invalidation, one coarse topology generation and typed plane-scoped invalidation on semantic result, causal-use receipts, hit rate, invalidation amplification, latency, RAM and crash/restart recovery.
caveats: The dependency ground truth is synthetic and declared by the experiment; it does not prove current Frank exposes same-epoch topology mutations.
No target-VPS runtime path, real Frank episode, GWT outcome or recovery path was executed in this experiment.
The result supports a compiler/cache safety candidate, not Hyperposition truth, causal emergence, consciousness or effect authority.
